name: South Korea
targetIntake: September 2027 — Korea's Fall intake (May 2027 IB session)
tagline: A separate international track, and an academic year that starts in March
summary: Korean universities run a completely separate admissions track for applicants who did all of their schooling outside Korea — usually called the 'Overseas Korean and Foreigner' or 'Special Admission' route — and an IB Diploma is a normal qualification inside it. You are not competing against Korean students who sat the Suneung; you are competing in a small international pool, assessed on your transcript, essays and an interview. Two things shape everything else. The Korean academic year starts in March, so the intake a May 2027 IB candidate can actually enter is the smaller September one, applied for in the first half of 2027 on predicted grades. And fully English-taught degrees are concentrated in a handful of places: Yonsei's Underwood International College, KAIST, parts of Korea University and Sungkyunkwan, and the Songdo international campuses. Outside those, 'taught in English' often means a mixed programme where Korean creeps back in after first year.
whyConsider: Yonsei's Underwood International College is a genuine full-English liberal-arts college inside a major research university: 16 majors across three divisions, roughly 3,000 students from more than 70 countries.
The international admissions track is document-and-interview based, which suits an IB student who writes well, and it is separate from the brutal domestic Suneung competition.
KAIST exempts scholarship holders from tuition for eight semesters and pays a monthly living allowance, decided from the admission application with no separate form to fill in.
KAIST teaches essentially all of its undergraduate programme in English and is one of Asia's strongest science and engineering universities.
Seoul is genuinely affordable compared with Tokyo, Singapore or Hong Kong once you are out of the central districts, and student dormitories are cheap and widely available.
watchOuts: The Korean academic year starts in March, and the March intake is the main one. For a May 2027 IB candidate it is not an option — you cannot matriculate in March 2027 with a diploma you sit exams for in May. The two real choices are September 2027, the smaller Fall intake, or March 2028 with results in hand.

Every deadline that matters falls before 6 July 2027. KAIST's regular round for September 2027 closes on 14 January 2027 and decides on 25 March; Yonsei UIC's second round runs in March 2027 and decides in June. Predicted grades do all the work, and what each university does with a conditional place when results arrive is set institution by institution and is not established here.

The Global Korea Scholarship's Embassy Track is closed to Danish citizens. The 2027 guidelines invite 74 countries and Denmark is not one of them, and no Korean embassy in Denmark appears in the guidelines' own contact list. Only the University Track's UIC Program is open — science and engineering at thirteen named universities, none of them Yonsei, KAIST, Seoul National or Korea University.

A May 2027 IB graduate is not eligible for the 2027 GKS round at all, because it requires a graduation certificate by 31 December 2026. The round to plan for is 2028, expected to open around September 2027.

Check very carefully what 'English-taught' means at each university. Korea University and Sungkyunkwan advertise high English-medium course percentages, but that is a university-wide average, not a guarantee that your specific major runs in English for four years.

Yonsei UIC now requires proof of English proficiency from every applicant from the 2027 academic year, and its test exemption is written by country rather than by language of instruction — Denmark is not on the list. Do not assume an English-medium IB exempts you anywhere; ask in writing.
Only one Korean tuition figure could be read from an official page in this pass, and the page carried no price year. Treat every other cost here as unresearched rather than absent.
Denmark's SU works differently for a full degree outside the EU/EEA. Confirm with su.dk before budgeting.

ibRecognition.subjectLevelRule: There is no national rule. Each university reads the IB transcript inside its own international admission track, and the category that matters is the one for applicants who completed the entire curriculum outside Korea — Seoul National University calls it 글로벌인재특별전형 II, 'those who completed the entire curriculum overseas'. Whether any institution publishes a minimum IB point score was not established in this pass.
ibRecognition.gradeConversion: No national conversion. Each university reads the IB transcript directly within its international admissions track. The Global Korea Scholarship publishes its own thresholds — 80 per cent on a 100-point scale, or the top 20 per cent of the class, or a CGPA at or above 2.64/4.0, 2.80/4.3, 2.91/4.5 or 3.23/5.0 — but says nothing about how an IB transcript is read against them.
notes: The relevant Korean category is the '12-year education completed entirely outside Korea' route, which an IB Diploma from a Danish gymnasium satisfies. This is the track that removes the Suneung from the equation.
Some universities also accept the IB as proof of English, others insist on IELTS or TOEFL even from an English-medium school. Ask each admissions office directly.
Minimum and typical IB scores were not published on any page we could read. Anything you see quoted on an agent site should be treated as unverified.
A Korean-language requirement (TOPIK) usually applies only to Korean-taught programmes, but a few English-taught degrees ask for a TOPIK level by graduation. Check the small print.

portal.name: No central portal for the international track — apply direct to each university. Study in Korea (NIIED) is the official information portal.

deadlines.label: KAIST Regular Admissions, Fall 2027 entry
deadlines.notes: Opened 10 November 2026. The recommendation letter has a later deadline of its own, 21 January 2027. Decision 25 March 2027 — five months before IB results.

deadlines.label: Yonsei UIC 2nd Round, Fall 2027 entry
deadlines.notes: UIC publishes this round as "March, 2027" and marks the column TBD; interview and admission notification are given as June 2027. This is the round a May 2027 IB candidate uses. The 1st Round, for the March 2027 intake, closed on 22 September 2026.

deadlines.label: Korea University Fall 2027 application
deadlines.notes: Marked TBA on Korea University's international admission guide in September 2026. Its Spring 2027 equivalent ran 3 to 31 August 2026. Submitted through Uwayapply, not the university's own site.

deadlines.label: Embassy Track online application, 2027 GKS-U
deadlines.notes: Closed to Danish citizens: the 2027 guidelines invite 74 countries and Denmark is not one. Also closed to a May 2027 IB candidate of any nationality, because the round requires a graduation certificate by 31 December 2026. Recorded so that neither fact has to be rediscovered.

deadlines.label: University Track application, 2027 GKS-U
deadlines.notes: NIIED gives the track as September to November 2026 and says each university sets its own period, method and documents. The UIC Program is the only part of GKS open to all nationalities. No individual university deadline was read in this pass.

deadlines.label: First international round for the March 2028 intake
deadlines.notes: The alternative to September 2027, and the only Korean intake a May 2027 IB candidate can apply to holding an actual diploma. Nothing is published yet. In the 2027 cycle the equivalent rounds ran 6–9 July 2026 at Seoul National, 3–31 August 2026 at Korea University and 26 August–22 September 2026 at Yonsei UIC; none of those dates is carried forward here.

steps: From September 2026, check each target university's 'Admission for International Students' or 'Overseas Korean and Foreigner Special Admission' page — this is a different page from the domestic admissions site, and often a different subdomain.
Confirm whether your intended major genuinely runs in English for all four years, in writing, from the department rather than the marketing page.

Decide between September 2027 and March 2028. March 2027 is not available to you: it is Korea's main intake, but its rounds closed in the summer and early autumn of 2026 and it starts before you have sat your exams.
Prepare the standard international pack: IB transcript and predicted grades, a self-introduction essay, a study plan, references, proof of your and your parents' nationality, and financial evidence.

If you want the Global Korea Scholarship, read the invited-country list first. On a Danish passport only the University Track's UIC Program is open, and it is science and engineering at thirteen named universities. Applying on more than one track voids the application.
Once admitted, the university issues a Certificate of Admission; you apply for a D-2 student visa at the Korean embassy and register for an Alien Registration Card within 90 days of arrival.
application.selectionNotes: Selection in the international track is holistic: transcript, essays, references and usually an online interview. Because the applicant pool is small and separate, strong IB students are often competitive at universities that would be unreachable through the domestic route. UIC, KAIST and SNU are nonetheless genuinely selective.

language.englishTaughtBachelors: Concentrated rather than widespread. Yonsei UIC (16 majors), KAIST (essentially the whole undergraduate programme), and selected tracks at Korea University, Sungkyunkwan, Ewha, Hanyang and the Songdo international campuses. National totals were not verified.
language.englishProof: Varies by university. Some accept IB English or an English-medium schooling certificate; others require IELTS or TOEFL regardless. Specific scores not verified.
notes: You do not need Korean to be admitted to an English-taught programme, but you will need it to live well, to work part-time and to do internships.
Most universities run free or heavily subsidised Korean language classes for their own international students.
The Global Korea Scholarship includes a full year of Korean language training before the degree begins — one of the reasons it is worth more than its cash value.

tuitionEuEea.value: Korea does not differentiate by nationality — international students pay the same published tuition as Korean students at most universities. See tuitionNonEu.

notes: One figure was read from an official page in this pass and it is KAIST's: tuition of 3,433,000 KRW a semester, national health insurance at 458,340 KRW and on-campus housing at 664,000 KRW, all per semester. KAIST's page states no academic year for them, so they are held at needs-review rather than shown as current. Nothing here is carried to any other institution.

The structure to expect: tuition is charged per semester and varies sharply by faculty, with medicine and engineering highest and humanities lowest. Private universities (Yonsei, Korea, Sungkyunkwan, Ewha, Hanyang) charge considerably more than the national universities.
Most universities award an automatic partial tuition scholarship to admitted international students, often tied to grades — ask what the standing award is before comparing sticker prices.

Dormitory places are cheap and usually available to first-year international students. Off-campus renting in Korea involves a large jeonse or wolse key deposit that is difficult to raise from abroad — take the dormitory.

funding: Global Korea Scholarship (GKS), run by NIIED — the flagship government scholarship for undergraduate degrees, and smaller than it looks from Denmark. The 2027 round covers tuition of up to 5m KRW a semester, a Korean language year costing 5.2m KRW, airfare, and an allowance of 13.56m KRW in the language year and 14.4m KRW a year during the degree, over five to seven years. The Embassy Track invites 74 countries and Denmark is not among them; only the University Track's UIC Program, science and engineering at thirteen named universities, is open to a Danish citizen. A May 2027 IB graduate is in any case ineligible for the 2027 round, which requires a graduation certificate by 31 December 2026 — the round to plan for is 2028.

University international-student scholarships: most Korean universities award an automatic tuition reduction to admitted international students, frequently renewable on GPA. Ask each admissions office for the standing rate, since it changes the real price materially.

The KAIST Scholarship exempts an admitted international undergraduate from tuition for eight semesters and pays 350,000 KRW a month plus medical insurance. There is no separate application — you tick a box on the admission form — and it is held on a GPA above 2.7 out of 4.3 after the first year.
Yonsei, Korea University and SNU all operate named merit awards for high-performing international entrants. Details not established here.
Danish SU: a full degree outside the EU/EEA follows separate rules. Check su.dk before assuming SU travels with you.
Part-time work is permitted on a D-2 visa with permission from the immigration office, but the hour limits and the requirement for a TOPIK level vary — confirm with Korea Immigration Service.
workRights: Students on a D-2 visa may work part-time only after obtaining permission from the immigration office, with hour limits that in recent years have been tied to Korean language proficiency (TOPIK level) and academic standing. Specific limits were not verified in this research — confirm with the Korea Immigration Service before relying on part-time earnings.
residency: EU citizenship gives no shortcut. You need a D-2 student visa, applied for at the Korean embassy in Copenhagen with the Certificate of Admission issued by your university, proof of funds, and a criminal-record and tuberculosis check. Within 90 days of arrival you register for an Alien Registration Card at the local immigration office — you cannot open a bank account or get a phone contract without it.
housing: University dormitories are the standard and by far the easiest route for a first-year international student: cheap, on campus, and allocated with the admission. The private market in Seoul requires a large up-front deposit (jeonse or wolse) that is impractical to arrange from Denmark. Apply for the dormitory the moment your offer arrives — places at Yonsei and Korea University are oversubscribed.
healthcare: International students staying more than six months are enrolled in Korea's National Health Insurance Service, with a monthly premium deducted or billed. It is compulsory and it is good — Korean healthcare is fast and inexpensive at the point of use. Your Danish EHIC does not apply.

institutions.name: Yonsei University — Underwood International College
institutions.englishBachelors: 16 majors, all taught in English, across three divisions: Underwood (comparative literature, economics, international studies, political science and IR, life science and biotechnology); Humanities Arts and Social Sciences (Asian studies, culture and design management, information and interaction design, creative technology management, justice and civil leadership, quantitative risk management, science technology and policy, sustainable development and cooperation); and Integrated Science and Engineering (nano science, energy and environmental science, bio-convergence).
institutions.note: The single best English-taught undergraduate option in Korea: a liberal-arts college of about 3,000 students from more than 70 countries, inside one of the country's three most prestigious universities. First two years are on the Songdo campus near Incheon, then Sinchon in central Seoul.

institutions.name: Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology
institutions.englishBachelors: Essentially the entire undergraduate programme is taught in English across science, engineering, business and the College of Liberal Arts and Convergence Science.
institutions.note: Korea's MIT, in the science city of Daejeon. Undergraduates enter without declaring a major and choose at the end of first year. Known for very generous scholarship support for admitted students, including international ones — confirm the current terms with the admissions office.

institutions.name: Seoul National University
institutions.englishBachelors: Limited. SNU runs a large share of its graduate teaching in English, but undergraduate English-medium provision is partial and varies by college. Verify programme by programme before applying.
institutions.note: The most prestigious university in Korea and the hardest to get into domestically — which makes the separate international track unusually valuable. The weakness for an IB student is that the undergraduate curriculum is not systematically English-medium.

institutions.name: Korea University
institutions.englishBachelors: A substantial share of courses are taught in English, particularly in Business, International Studies, Political Science and Economics, but few majors are guaranteed 100% English for four years. Verify with the department.
institutions.note: One of the 'SKY' trio with SNU and Yonsei, with the strongest law and business alumni network in the country and a famously intense campus culture. Its Division of International Studies is the most reliably English-taught part. Applications run through Uwayapply, a shared national platform, rather than the university's own site.

institutions.name: Sungkyunkwan University
institutions.englishBachelors: Global Business Administration, Global Economics, Global Leader (law and policy) and several science and engineering tracks are taught substantially or wholly in English. Verify individually.
institutions.note: Traces itself to a Confucian academy founded in 1398, making it nominally the oldest university in East Asia, but it is funded by Samsung and is aggressively modern — its semiconductor and software programmes come with direct Samsung recruitment pipelines.

institutions.name: Ewha Womans University
institutions.englishBachelors: Division of International Studies and Scranton College's Honors Program are taught in English; other faculties are largely Korean-medium.
institutions.note: The largest women's university in the world and a central institution in modern Korean history. Its Scranton Honors Program and Division of International Studies are the English-medium entry points; admission is open to women only.

institutions.name: Hanyang University
institutions.englishBachelors: Selected engineering, business and international studies tracks. Not verified.
institutions.note: Korea's leading private engineering university and the source of a remarkable share of the country's construction and heavy-industry leadership. Strong start-up culture and an unusually practical engineering curriculum.

institutions.name: Pohang University of Science and Technology
institutions.englishBachelors: Undergraduate teaching is substantially in English, but the programme is small and international undergraduate intake is limited. Verify before applying.
institutions.note: A tiny, research-intensive science institute founded by the POSCO steel company, with about 1,400 undergraduates and a famously high staff-to-student ratio. KAIST's rival, in a coastal industrial city rather than a big student town.

institutions.name: Sogang University
institutions.englishBachelors: Selected business, economics and international studies courses. Not verified.
institutions.note: A small Jesuit university with a reputation for rigour out of proportion to its size, and the best-known Korean-language institute in the country if you want to learn the language properly alongside a degree.

institutions.name: Kyung Hee University
institutions.englishBachelors: College of International Studies and selected hospitality and business tracks. Not verified.
institutions.note: Large and internationally oriented, with one of the biggest international student populations in Korea and a genuinely unusual strength in hospitality management and traditional Korean medicine.

institutions.name: Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology
institutions.englishBachelors: UNIST teaches its undergraduate programme in English as a matter of institutional policy. Verify the current position with admissions.
institutions.note: The youngest of Korea's science institutes and the most explicitly English-medium, in Ulsan — Hyundai's industrial city. Undergraduates enter undeclared and choose a track after a common first year.

institutions.name: Gwangju Institute of Science and Technology
institutions.englishBachelors: The undergraduate College teaches in English with a common curriculum before major selection. Verify current policy.
institutions.note: A small research institute in the south-west with a liberal-arts-inflected science curriculum: every undergraduate takes humanities alongside the science core. About 200 undergraduates a year.

institutions.name: Handong Global University
institutions.englishBachelors: A large share of teaching is in English, including the International Studies, Languages and Literature and Global Management tracks. Not verified.
institutions.note: A Christian university with an explicitly international mission and an unusual undeclared-entry structure: students choose a major at the end of the first year and may double-major freely. Considerably more accessible than the Seoul universities.

institutions.name: Chung-Ang University
institutions.englishBachelors: Selected business, economics and international tracks. Not verified.
institutions.note: The leading Korean university for film, drama and performing arts — a large share of Korean screen actors and directors trained here. If the draw is Korean cultural industries rather than engineering, this is the address.
